+# .claude/data/profiles.yaml — `loa.profile` defaults (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §3.5;
+# DEC-0143, DEC-0152).
+#
+# One knob, `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` in .loa.config.yaml, sets the
+# defaults of the optional surfaces below as a set. Resolution, per key
+# (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh `loa_knob`):
+#   1. the key set explicitly in .loa.config.yaml wins;
+#   2. else the selected profile's value (unset or unknown profile → standard);
+#   3. else the caller's fallback — never reached for a key listed here,
+#      because every profile defines every key (tests/unit/profile-lib.bats).
+#
+# `standard` is the post-cycle-129 example default of each key, written out
+# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json records how each value was
+# captured). The two guardrail keys read false here because cycle-129 changed
+# their example default (D-4.4, DEC-0161): a migration item, not a profile effect.
+#
+# No floor key may appear here. The floor config keys are listed once, in
+# .claude/data/floor.yaml `floor_keys`; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats fails if a
+# profile names one, and profile-lib.sh ignores such a key with a WARN.
+# `interview.pacing` is not a profile key: `rounds` is already the default and
+# the key would not discriminate between profiles.
+schema_version: 1
+
+profiles:
+  lean:
+    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: false
+    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
+    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: false
+    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: false
+    guardrails.input.enabled: false
+    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
+    invisible_retrospective.enabled: false
+    structured_handoff.enabled: false
+    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
+  standard:

+    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
+    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
+    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
+    guardrails.input.enabled: false
+    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
+    invisible_retrospective.enabled: true
+    structured_handoff.enabled: false
+    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
+  full:
+    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: true
+    decisions.surface_at_session_start: true
+    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
+    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
+    guardrails.input.enabled: true

-# perf pass-7 (2026-07-05, skill-loop): O(n) -> O(delta) on the growing
-# state file. The per-call cost was O(session length): the single jq
-# --rawfile'd ALL of karpathy-task-state.jsonl (files_modified set +
-# tool_call_count) and awk re-scanned the whole file for the running total
-# — measured 20ms at n=500 entries, 36ms at n=5000, 111ms at n=20000.
-# Aggregates are now cached at .run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg and
-# folded INCREMENTALLY over only the appended bytes. Design notes:
-#   - Cache format (9 lines, no trailing newline; the set line is LAST so
-#     the bash reader never has to load it — reads stop at line 8):
-#       1 key    "<dev>:<ino>:<abs-state-path>" (post-append stat identity;
-#                the abs-path component blocks cross-repo/worktree
-#                contamination through shared relative KARPATHY_TASK_STATE
-#                names; dev:ino rotates on rename/replace rotation)
-#       2 offset bytes processed; ALWAYS ends at a '\n' line boundary and
-#                always == the file size at the last cache write
-#       3 mtime  stat %y (ns) at the last cache write
-#       4 pois   1 when any processed line poisons files_modified (the
-#                wholesale try/catch -> 0 semantic); append-only files
-#                never un-poison, so the flag is monotonic
-#       5 nl     newline count through offset (tool_calls == nl + 1)
-#       6 sum    mawk running lines_changed total through offset — always a
-#                bash-integer product; caching requires ^-?[0-9]{1,15}$ so
-#                the decimal round-trips the awk double EXACTLY
-#       7 count  |set| (files_modified == count when the current file is
-#                already a member — the steady state)
-#       8 token  the hook's own last-appended state line (newline-free by
-#                construction, 1..1024 bytes) — the prefix-integrity probe
-#       9 set    compact JSON array: unique .file values through offset
-#                INCLUDING the hook's own appended entry (jq `unique`
-#                ordering; all members verified strings at write time)
-#   - Set-membership shortcut (the real repo holds 438 unique files across
-#     646 entries — ~32KB of set — so parsing + re-unique-ing it per call
-#     would eat the win): the warm jq tests membership TEXTUALLY on the
-#     compact set line — needle "," + ($file|tojson) + "," against
-#     "," + inner + ",". SOUNDNESS: in a compact jq array of strings a
-#     quote inside an element is always escaped (backslash-quote), so a
-#     bare  ," / ",  pair can only occur at element boundaries — a match
-#     PROVES membership. A false NEGATIVE merely takes the exact
-#     parse+unique path. On a hit (repeat file, the steady state) the set
-#     is never parsed and never re-serialized: the emit uses an "="
-#     passthrough sentinel and bash rewrites the bytes it already read
-#     (set lines always start with "[", so "=" is unambiguous). All nine
-#     lines are read from ONE fd, so a concurrent cache mv cannot tear the
-#     read (the fd pins the old inode).
-#   - Per call: ONE GNU-first stat. size==offset AND mtime==cached ⇒ FAST
-#     path (no state read at all; aggregates are current). size>offset ⇒
-#     DELTA path: `tail -c +(offset-len(token))` streams token+delta into
-#     the SAME single jq via --rawfile procsub; the token must match
-#     byte-for-byte at the recorded boundary or the call falls back to a
-#     full rescan. The lines_changed fold reuses THE SAME awk program on a
-#     second tail procsub (`NR==1 {next}` skips the token line) seeded with
-#     `-v init=<cached sum>` in BEGIN — same left-to-right association as
-#     the full-file scan, so the printed total is bit-identical (mawk
-#     strtod-prefix semantics on malformed/truncated lines are preserved by
-#     construction: it IS the same awk on the same line bytes; line sets
-#     decompose exactly because offset always sits on a '\n' boundary).
-#     ANY other relation (size<offset, mtime anomaly at equal size, key
-#     mismatch, corrupt/short/unreadable cache, token mismatch, U+FFFD in
-#     the delta = jq's invalid-UTF-8 replacement marker, non-array cached
-#     set) ⇒ full rescan through the ORIGINAL code path.
-#   - COLD path (no/invalid cache): the ORIGINAL jq program and ORIGINAL
-#     awk command run VERBATIM; the cache is rebuilt by a separate builder
-#     jq that re-reads the file POST-append, so cached aggregates are a
-#     true full-scan snapshot. Builder guards: no U+FFFD, utf8bytelength ==
-#     post-append stat size (raced growth ⇒ skip), content ends with the
-#     hook's own entry as a standalone line (a pre-append unterminated
-#     final line glues our entry into a hybrid line — computing THIS call
-#     stays correct, but the snapshot is only cacheable once the tail of
-#     the file is again a clean self-written line), all set members
-#     strings. Cold-path sum consistency: cache write additionally
-#     requires post-size == pre-size + len(entry)+1 (nothing else appended
-#     between the pre-stat and our append).
-#   - WARM path token-mismatch/corrupt-set anomalies keep the payload
-#     fields already extracted (stdin is consumed) and recompute
-#     files_modified/tool_call_count with an auxiliary jq over the full
-#     state PRE-append — the exact original expressions — plus the
-#     ORIGINAL awk; observable output is full-rescan-identical.
-#   - The hook's own append is folded into the cache (offset covers it;
-#     set gains the current file; nl+1; sum = the emitted running_total),
-#     so the next call's delta contains only genuinely new bytes.
-#   - Bounds / permanent fallbacks (silent, output identical): cached-set
-#     serialization > 64KiB ⇒ cache deleted, never rewritten while
-#     oversized (full-scan mode); own entry > 1024 bytes ⇒ cache write
-#     skipped; sum outside ±15 digits ⇒ skipped; awk or tail missing from
-#     PATH ⇒ whole feature disabled (a FAST hit would otherwise diverge
-#     from the old `awk … || echo 0` fallback total).
-#   - Size gate (KARPATHY_STATE_CACHE_MIN, default 262144 bytes): below it
-#     the ORIGINAL path runs end-to-end with the ORIGINAL spawn count
-#     (census: 3 = stat, jq, awk on both sides — the pre-stat rides the
-#     combined config stat) and no cache is written; the machinery engages

-#     warm-served file is always above the gate too (no
-#     serve-without-write staleness loop).
-#   - Concurrency: cache writes are atomic ($$-temp + mv -f -T; last
-#     writer wins; readers never see torn files). A concurrent appender
-#     between our read and our append makes the post-append size differ

-#     envelope, deterministic inputs are byte-identical.
-#   - Trust: same posture as pass-6 — anyone who can write
-#     .run/perf-cache/ can already write .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl,

-#     strictly harder (must match live stat identity + token bytes). The
-#     hook is non-blocking (warn-only) by design.

-#     bump the cache filename version (v1 -> v2); the key deliberately
-#     excludes program text.

-#     no-ops (exit 0) where the old code would have processed — one lost

+# =============================================================================
+# FR-6 heredoc consumer classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1; knob
+# destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier, default true; false = the
+# pre-cycle scan, i.e. only the #1245 quoted-cat scrub below).
+# Defined BEFORE the bash-version guard and the stdin read so another script
+# can source this file with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 and call
+#   _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   → prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>               → exit 0 iff nonexec
+# Bash 3.2 compatible (no ${x,,}, no mapfile, no associative arrays) and safe
+# under a caller's `set -u`.
+#
+# Grammar (literal command text; no alias or function expansion; CRLF folded
+# to LF). The command is walked line by line; a line holding an unquoted
+# `<<` / `<<-` (not `<<<`) is a heredoc header, the body runs to the first
+# line equal to the delimiter (leading tabs stripped for `<<-`). FULL SCAN
+# (the whole command as today) on: any other control character, a header the
+# tokenizer cannot read (open quote, trailing backslash, comment), more than
+# one heredoc on a header, a delimiter that is not a plain word ('W', "W",
+# \W or W with W in [A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]; `$X` is a variable delimiter), or a
+# missing terminator. Per heredoc the class is:
+#   interpreter — body scanned exactly as today: the header holds `$(`, a
+#     backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a paren or brace group or a shell keyword; it
+#     continues on the next line (`|`, `&&`, `||` last) or an earlier line
+#     opened a substitution, group, quote or pipe; a member of the heredoc's
+#     pipeline is a shell, interpreter, wrapper that runs its argument or SQL
+#     runner (_bdb_hd_is_interp, _bdb_hd_is_runner); an allowlisted form
+#     carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag (-c, -e, -x clusters, --exec,
+#     --eval, --command, in-place); a write target is executable content
+#     (_bdb_hd_exec_dest: script extension, .claude/hooks, .claude/settings*
+#     .json, .git/hooks, .git/config, rc/profile files, /etc, a bin dir or a
+#     directory on PATH, or any non-literal path); the first body line is a
+#     shebang; the body holds `<<` (nested); a target's basename appears
+#     elsewhere in the command outside the safe readers (_bdb_hd_same_line_exec:
+#     `bash x`, `./x`, `source x`, `. x`, `chmod +x x`, `exec x`, cp/mv …).
+#   nonexec — every pipeline member is an exact allowlisted form
+#     (_bdb_hd_member): cat, tee, printf, echo with plain-file or stdout sinks;
+#     gh pr|issue comment -F -; gh pr create --body-file -; git commit -F -;
+#     br create|update reading `-`; jq/yq without in-place; grep; sed -n with
+#     a print-only script; sort; wc. The body is then scanned PER SEGMENT
+#     (_bdb_hd_scan_body): each line split on ; && || | &, wrapper prefixes
+#     stripped (sudo command exec env nice time nohup builtin stdbuf ionice,
+#     a leading backslash, quote, paren or brace, assignments, an absolute
+#     path); a segment whose command word is a fence verb (rm git find dd
+#     mkfs* shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql DROP
+#     DELETE TRUNCATE) is kept on its own line for the normal rules, other
+#     segments are dropped. The body falls back to a full scan when it holds
+#     `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(` under an unquoted delimiter, or a segment
+#     word is an interpreter or wrapper, or a variable (`$x -rf /`; such a
+#     segment is ALSO scanned as rm, git and kubectl with the same arguments).
+#     Special case (the #1245 scrub): a standalone quoted-delimiter `cat`
+#     whose header is exactly `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops the whole body.
+#   none — the consumer is on neither list: full scan.
+# Documented gap: a body written to a plain file by one command and executed
+# by a LATER command is outside a per-command fence (the Write tool shares it).
+# =============================================================================
+_bdb_hd_op_re='^[0-9]*(<<<|<<-|&>>|<<|>>|>[|]|&&|[|][|]|[|]&|&>|<>|>&[0-9-]*|<&[0-9-]*|;;|;|&|[|]|<|>|[(]|[)])$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dw='^[A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dsq="^'([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ddq='^"([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)"$'
+_bdb_hd_re_dbs='^\\([A-Za-z0-9_.+:@%-]+)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_psq="^'([^']*)'\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pdq="^\"([^\"\$\`\\\\]*)\"\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_pbare="^[^'\"\$\`\\\\]+\$"
+_bdb_hd_re_ctl=$'[\x01-\x08\x0b-\x1f\x7f]'
+_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'
+_bdb_hd_re_exlong='^--(exec|eval|command|in-?place)'
+_bdb_hd_re_ext='\.(sh|bash|zsh|ksh|csh|fish|py|pyw|rb|pl|pm|js|mjs|cjs|ts|mts|cts|ps1|psm1|php|lua|tcl|command|bat|cmd)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_sys='(^|/)(\.claude/hooks(/|$)|\.claude/settings[^/]*\.json$|\.git/hooks(/|$)|\.git/config$|\.gitconfig$|\.ssh/rc$|\.config/(fish|zsh|bash|git)/|s?bin/[^/]+$)'
+_bdb_hd_re_rc='(^|/)\.(bashrc|bash_profile|bash_login|bash_logout|profile|zshrc|zshenv|zprofile|zlogin|zlogout|kshrc|mkshrc|cshrc|tcshrc|login|logout|envrc)$'
+_bdb_hd_re_sedp='^(([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/)(,([0-9]+|[$]|/[^/]*/))?)?p$'
+_bdb_hd_re_assign='^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*='
+_bdb_hd_re_varw='^[$]([{]|[A-Za-z_])'
+_bdb_hd_re_knob='^[[:space:]]+heredoc_classifier:[[:space:]]*["'"'"']?([A-Za-z]+)["'"'"']?[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$'
+
+# Shells, interpreters and wrappers that run their argument or stdin.
+_bdb_hd_is_interp() {
+  case "$1" in
+    bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh|mksh|ash|fish|csh|tcsh|busybox|python|python[0-9]*|pypy*|node|nodejs|deno|bun|ruby|irb|perl|php|lua|luajit|tclsh|wish|expect|pwsh|powershell|osascript|Rscript) return 0 ;;
+    eval|source|.|exec|command|builtin|time|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|make|gmake|m4|ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|gdb) return 0 ;;
+    sudo|doas|su|runuser|env|xargs|parallel|timeout|nohup|nice|ionice|setsid|stdbuf|chroot|unshare|nsenter|ssh|docker|podman|kubectl|find|watch|script) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# The SQL runners of the FR-1.4/5/6 precondition (same list).
+_bdb_hd_is_runner() {
+  case "$1" in
+    psql|pgcli|mysql|mariadb|mysqlsh|sqlite3|sqlcmd|sqlplus|isql|usql|litecli|duckdb|clickhouse|clickhouse-client|cockroach|bq|wrangler|prisma|supabase|drizzle-kit|knex|sequelize|typeorm|flyway|liquibase|dbmate|goose|sqitch|rails|manage.py|artisan|alembic|dbt|atlas|mongosh|sqlx) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# Command words the fence's own rules match.
+_bdb_hd_is_destructive() {
+  case "$1" in
+    rm|git|find|dd|shred|truncate|kubectl|terraform|aws|gcloud|psql|mysql|mkfs|mkfs.*) return 0 ;;
+    [Dd][Rr][Oo][Pp]|[Dd][Ee][Ll][Ee][Tt][Ee]|[Tt][Rr][Uu][Nn][Cc][Aa][Tt][Ee]) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+# Readers that may name a heredoc's target elsewhere on the line.
+_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader() {
+  case "$1" in
+    cat|ls|wc|head|tail|grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|diff|cmp|stat|file|test|'['|echo|printf|sort|uniq|jq|yq|git|gh|br|mkdir|touch|realpath|readlink|basename|dirname|du|md5sum|sha1sum|sha256sum|shasum|b2sum|cksum) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_tokenize <line> → _bdb_hd_tok[] (words keep their quotes; operators
+# are separate tokens, an fd number joins its redirect). Returns 1 when the
+# line cannot be read: open quote, trailing backslash, unquoted comment.
+_bdb_hd_tokenize() {
+  local s="${1:-}" n i=0 ch tok="" q="" have=0 op cand
+  n=${#s}
+  _bdb_hd_tok=()
+  while (( i < n )); do
+    ch="${s:i:1}"
+    if [[ -n "$q" ]]; then
+      tok="$tok$ch"
+      if [[ "$q" == "'" ]]; then
+        [[ "$ch" == "'" ]] && q=""
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '\' ]]; then
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        i=$((i + 1)); tok="$tok${s:i:1}"
+      elif [[ "$ch" == '"' ]]; then
+        q=""
+      fi
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    case "$ch" in
+      "'"|'"') q="$ch"; tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '\')
+        (( i + 1 < n )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch${s:i+1:1}"; have=1; i=$((i + 2)) ;;
+      ' '|$'\t')
+        if (( have )); then _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"; tok=""; have=0; fi
+        i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      '#')
+        (( have )) || return 1
+        tok="$tok$ch"; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+      ';'|'&'|'|'|'<'|'>'|'('|')')
+        op=""
+        for cand in '<<<' '<<-' '&>>' '<<' '>>' '>|' '&&' '||' '|&' '&>' '<>' '>&' '<&' ';;' ';' '&' '|' '<' '>' '(' ')'; do
+          if [[ "${s:i:${#cand}}" == "$cand" ]]; then op="$cand"; break; fi
+        done
+        i=$((i + ${#op}))
+        if [[ "$op" == '>&' || "$op" == '<&' ]]; then
+          while (( i < n )) && [[ "${s:i:1}" == [0-9-] ]]; do op="$op${s:i:1}"; i=$((i + 1)); done
+        fi
+        if (( have )); then
+          if [[ "$tok" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$op" == '<'* || "$op" == '>'* ]]; then
+            op="$tok$op"
+          else
+            _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+          fi
+          tok=""; have=0
+        fi
+        _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$op" ;;
+      *) tok="$tok$ch"; have=1; i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  [[ -z "$q" ]] || return 1
+  (( have )) && _bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}]="$tok"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_unq_path <word> → _hd_up; returns 1 for a non-literal path (an
+# expansion, an escape, mixed quoting) or an empty one.
+_bdb_hd_unq_path() {
+  _hd_up=""
+  if [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq ]] || [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]]; then
+    _hd_up="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+  elif [[ "${1:-}" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pbare ]]; then
+    _hd_up="$1"
+  else
+    return 1
+  fi
+  [[ -n "$_hd_up" ]]
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_exec_dest <unquoted path> → 0 when a write there is executable
+# content (or cannot be judged).
+_bdb_hd_exec_dest() {
+  local p="${1:-}" d e b old_ifs
+  case "$p" in
+    *'*'*|*'?'*|*'['*|*'{'*|'~'|'~'[!/]*|'') return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  [[ "$p" == '~/'* ]] && p="${HOME:-}/${p#'~/'}"
+  b="${p##*/}"
+  [[ "$b" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ext ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sys || "$p" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_rc ]] && return 0
+  [[ "$p" == /etc/* ]] && return 0
+  if [[ "$p" == /* ]]; then d="${p%/*}"; [[ -n "$d" ]] || d="/"
+  elif [[ "$p" == */* ]]; then d="${PWD:-.}/${p%/*}"
+  else d="${PWD:-.}"
+  fi
+  old_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=':'
+  for e in ${PATH:-}; do
+    [[ -z "$e" || "$e" == "." ]] && e="${PWD:-.}"
+    [[ "$e" != "/" ]] && e="${e%/}"
+    if [[ "$d" == "$e" ]]; then IFS="$old_ifs"; return 0; fi
+  done
+  IFS="$old_ifs"
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_member <tokens…> → _hd_mcls (interpreter|nonexec|none) for one
+# pipeline member; write targets are appended to _hd_dests.
+_bdb_hd_member() {
+  local -a toks argv
+  local t nxt i n stdout_files=0 a0 base fd stdin=0 ops=0 want="" has_n=0 script=""
+  toks=("$@"); n=${#toks[@]}; argv=()
+  _hd_mcls=none
+  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
+    t="${toks[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_op_re ]]; then
+      case "$t" in
+        *'<<<') return ;;
+        *'<<'|*'<<-') i=$((i + 1)); continue ;;
+        *'>&'[0-9]*|*'>&-'|*'<&'*) continue ;;
+        *'>'|*'>>'|*'>|'|*'>&'|'&>'|'&>>')

+          _bdb_hd_unq_path "$nxt" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }

+  base="${a0#\\}"; base="${base##*/}"

+    t="${argv[i]}"
+    if [[ "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exflag || "$t" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_exlong ]]; then _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; fi
+  done

+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in

+          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          *) _bdb_hd_unq_path "$t" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }

+        esac

+      done ;;
+    gh)

+        "pr create") want=" -F --body-file --title -t --base -B --head -H --repo -R --label -l --reviewer -r --assignee -a --milestone -m --project -p --template -T | --draft -d --fill --fill-first --fill-verbose --no-maintainer-edit --dry-run " ;;
+        *) return ;;
+      esac
+      for ((i = 3; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in

+          --*=*) [[ "${want%%|*}" == *" ${t%%=*} "* ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+          -*)

+          *) ops=$((ops + 1)); [[ "${argv[2]}" == comment && $ops -le 1 ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;

+    git)

+          -F|--file) i=$((i + 1)); [[ "${argv[i]:-}" == "-" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; stdin=1 ;;

+        case "$t" in
+          -d|--description|--body) [[ "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
+          -f|--file) [[ "${argv[1]}" == create && "${argv[i+1]:-}" == "-" ]] && stdin=1 ;;
+          --description=-|--body=-) stdin=1 ;;

+      (( stdin )) || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    jq|yq)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        # In-place flags: --inplace/--in-place, -i, -i=…, and any short-flag cluster holding an i
+        # (corpus D114/D115: `-i` alone did not match `-[A-Za-z]*i*`, which needs a letter before the i).
+        case "${argv[i]}" in --inplace|--in-place|-i*|-[A-Za-z]*i*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;; esac
+      done ;;
+    grep|egrep|fgrep) ;;
+    sed)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"

+          -n|--quiet|--silent) has_n=1 ;;
+          -E|-r|--regexp-extended|-s|--separate|-u|--unbuffered|-z|--null-data) ;;
+          -*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          *) if [[ -z "$script" ]]; then
+               script="$t"; [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_psq || "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_pdq ]] && script="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+               [[ "$script" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_sedp ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }
+             fi ;;
+        esac
+      done
+      (( has_n )) && [[ -n "$script" ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+    sort)
+      for ((i = 1; i < ${#argv[@]}; i++)); do
+        t="${argv[i]}"
+        case "$t" in
+          -o) i=$((i + 1)); _bdb_hd_unq_path "${argv[i]:-}" || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; }; _hd_dests[${#_hd_dests[@]}]="$_hd_up" ;;
+          -k|-t) i=$((i + 1)) ;;
+          -k*|-t*) ;;
+          --*) _hd_mcls=interpreter; return ;;
+          -*) [[ "$t" =~ ^-[bdfghiMnRrsuVz]+$ ]] || { _hd_mcls=interpreter; return; } ;;
+        esac
+      done ;;

+      done ;;

+
+# _bdb_hd_ctx_bad <line> → 0 when a line before (or the header itself) leaves
+# the next text inside a substitution, group, quote, compound command or
+# pipeline: a later heredoc there is interpreter-class.
+_bdb_hd_ctx_bad() {
+  local l="${1:-}" k last
+  case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) return 0 ;; esac
+  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$l" || return 0
+  for ((k = 0; k < ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}; k++)); do
+    case "${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}" in
+      '('|')'|'{'|'}'|do|done|then|else|elif|if|fi|while|until|for|case|esac|select|function|coproc) return 0 ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  (( ${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]} > 0 )) || return 1
+  last="${_bdb_hd_tok[${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}-1]}"
+  case "$last" in '|'|'|&'|'&&'|'||') return 0 ;; esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_header <line> — parse one header line. Sets _hd_ops (heredoc count,
+# -1 = unreadable), _hd_delim, _hd_quoted, _hd_tabs, _hd_cls, _hd_dests[],
+# _hd_pipe (pipeline id of the heredoc on this line).
+_bdb_hd_header() {
+  local line="${1:-}" k nt t opi=-1 w seg=0 pipe=0
+  local -a tpipe mtoks
+  _hd_ops=0 _hd_delim="" _hd_quoted=0 _hd_tabs=0 _hd_cls=none _hd_pipe=-1
+  _hd_dests=()
+  if ! _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"; then _hd_ops=-1; return; fi
+  nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
+  tpipe=()
+  for ((k = 0; k < nt; k++)); do
+    t="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"
+    case "$t" in
+      ';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')') pipe=$((pipe + 1)); tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
+      '|'|'|&') tpipe[k]=-1; continue ;;
+    esac
+    tpipe[k]=$pipe
+    if [[ "$t" =~ ^[0-9]*'<<'-?$ ]]; then _hd_ops=$((_hd_ops + 1)); opi=$k; fi
+  done
+  (( _hd_ops == 1 )) || return
+  w="${_bdb_hd_tok[opi+1]:-}"
+  [[ "${_bdb_hd_tok[opi]}" == *'<<-' ]] && _hd_tabs=1
+  if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dsq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ddq || "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dbs ]]; then
+    _hd_delim="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; _hd_quoted=1
+  elif [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_dw ]]; then
+    _hd_delim="$w"
+  else
+    _hd_ops=-1; return        # variable-expanded, mixed or missing delimiter
+  fi
+  _hd_pipe="${tpipe[opi]}"
+  if _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$line"; then _hd_cls=interpreter; return; fi
+  _bdb_hd_tokenize "$line"    # _bdb_hd_ctx_bad reused the token buffer
+  # Classify every member of the heredoc's pipeline; the most executing wins.
+  local cls=nonexec
+  k=0
+  while (( k < nt )); do
+    if [[ "${tpipe[k]}" != "$_hd_pipe" ]]; then k=$((k + 1)); continue; fi
+    mtoks=()
+    while (( k < nt )) && [[ "${tpipe[k]}" == "$_hd_pipe" ]]; do mtoks[${#mtoks[@]}]="${_bdb_hd_tok[k]}"; k=$((k + 1)); done
+    _bdb_hd_member "${mtoks[@]}"
+    case "$_hd_mcls" in
+      interpreter) cls=interpreter ;;
+      none) [[ "$cls" == interpreter ]] || cls=none ;;
+    esac
+    k=$((k + 1))
+  done
+  _hd_cls="$cls"
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_segword <segment> → _hd_w (command word after wrapper stripping,
+# quotes and an absolute path removed) and _hd_rest (the text after it).
+_bdb_hd_segword() {
+  local s="${1:-}" w guard=0
+  _hd_w="" _hd_rest=""
+  while (( guard < 64 )); do
+    guard=$((guard + 1))
+    s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+    [[ -n "$s" ]] || return
+    case "${s:0:1}" in
+      '('|'{'|'!'|'\'|'"'|"'") s="${s:1}"; continue ;;
+    esac
+    w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"
+    s="${s:${#w}}"
+    if [[ "$w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_assign ]]; then continue; fi
+    case "$w" in
+      sudo|doas|command|exec|env|nice|time|nohup|builtin|stdbuf|ionice)
+        while :; do
+          s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+          case "$s" in
+            -S|-S[[:space:]]*|--split-string*) _hd_w="sh"; _hd_rest="$s"; return ;;
+            -[ugnCphUrtTDc]|-[ugnCphUrtTDc][[:space:]]*)
+              s="${s:2}"; s="${s#"${s%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
+            -*) w="${s%%[[:space:]]*}"; s="${s:${#w}}" ;;
+            *) break ;;
+          esac
+        done
+        continue ;;
+    esac
+    w="${w%%[\"\']*}"
+    [[ "$w" == */* && "$w" != '$'* ]] && w="${w##*/}"
+    _hd_w="$w"; _hd_rest="$s"
+    return
+  done
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_scan_body <first> <last> <quoted> — per-segment scan of
+# _bdb_hd_L[first..last]. Sets _hd_kept (fence-verb segments, one per line),
+# _hd_synth (variable-command segments rewritten as rm/git/kubectl) and
+# _hd_full (1 = the body needs the full scan).
+_bdb_hd_scan_body() {
+  local k l t seg
+  _hd_kept="" _hd_synth="" _hd_full=0
+  for ((k = $1; k <= $2; k++)); do
+    l="${_bdb_hd_L[k]}"
+    [[ "$l" == *'<<'* ]] && _hd_full=1
+    if (( ! $3 )); then
+      case "$l" in *'$('*|*'`'*|*'<('*|*'>('*) _hd_full=1 ;; esac
+    fi
+    t="${l//'&&'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'||'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'|'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//';'/$'\n'}"; t="${t//'&'/$'\n'}"
+    while :; do
+      seg="${t%%$'\n'*}"
+      _bdb_hd_segword "$seg"
+      if [[ -n "$_hd_w" ]]; then
+        if [[ "$_hd_w" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_varw ]]; then
+          _hd_full=1
+          _hd_synth="${_hd_synth}rm${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"git${_hd_rest}"$'\n'"kubectl${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_destructive "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_kept="${_hd_kept}${_hd_w}${_hd_rest}"$'\n'
+        elif _bdb_hd_is_interp "$_hd_w" || _bdb_hd_is_runner "$_hd_w"; then
+          _hd_full=1
+        fi
+      fi
+      [[ "$t" == *$'\n'* ]] || break
+      t="${t#*$'\n'}"
+    done
+  done
+}
+
+# _bdb_hd_same_line_exec <basename> <header idx> <body first> <body last>
+# → 0 when the target is named anywhere else in the command outside a safe
+# reader (it may be executed, sourced, made executable, copied or moved).
+_bdb_hd_same_line_exec() {
+  local b="$1" hi="$2" bf="$3" bl="$4" k nt t u c cw seg_has pipe start j own
+  for ((k = 0; k < _bdb_hd_n; k++)); do
+    (( k >= bf && k <= bl )) && continue
+    [[ "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" == *"$b"* ]] || continue
+    _bdb_hd_tokenize "${_bdb_hd_L[k]}" || return 0
+    nt=${#_bdb_hd_tok[@]}
+    start=0 pipe=0
+    for ((j = 0; j <= nt; j++)); do
+      t="${_bdb_hd_tok[j]:-}"
+      if (( j < nt )) && ! [[ "$t" =~ ^(';'|';;'|'&'|'&&'|'||'|'('|')'|'|'|'|&')$ ]]; then continue; fi
+      # segment [start, j)
+      own=0
+      (( k == hi && pipe == _hd_pipe_saved )) && own=1
+      if (( ! own )); then
+        seg_has=0 cw=""
+        for ((c = start; c < j; c++)); do
+          u="${_bdb_hd_tok[c]}"; u="${u//[\"\']/}"; u="${u##*/}"
+          [[ "$u" == "$b" ]] && seg_has=1
+        done
+        if (( seg_has )); then
+          _bdb_hd_segword "${_bdb_hd_tok[*]:start:j-start}"
+          cw="$_hd_w"
+          if ! _bdb_hd_is_safe_reader "$cw" || [[ "$cw" == "$b" ]]; then return 0; fi
+        fi
+      fi
+      case "$t" in '|'|'|&') ;; *) pipe=$((pipe + 1)) ;; esac
+      start=$((j + 1))
+    done
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# _bdb_heredoc_scrub <command> — print the scrub copy (non-executing heredoc
+# bodies reduced to their fence-verb segments) and set _bdb_hd_class to the
+# most executing class seen (interpreter > none > nonexec; none if no heredoc).
+_bdb_heredoc_scrub() {
+  local text="${1:-}" out="" i j found l cls ctx=0 seen="" d first
+  _bdb_hd_class=none
+  text="${text//$'\r\n'/$'\n'}"
+  if [[ "$text" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_ctl ]]; then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+  text="${text%$'\n'}"
+  _bdb_hd_L=()
+  while IFS= read -r l; do _bdb_hd_L[${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}]="$l"; done <<< "$text"
+  _bdb_hd_n=${#_bdb_hd_L[@]}
+  i=0
+  while (( i < _bdb_hd_n )); do
+    l="${_bdb_hd_L[i]}"
+    if [[ "$l" != *'<<'* ]]; then
+      out="$out$l"$'\n'
+      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    _bdb_hd_header "$l"
+    if (( _hd_ops == 0 )); then
+      out="$out$l"$'\n'
+      (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+      i=$((i + 1)); continue
+    fi
+    if (( _hd_ops != 1 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+    found=-1
+    for ((j = i + 1; j < _bdb_hd_n; j++)); do
+      d="${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"
+      if (( _hd_tabs )); then while [[ "$d" == $'\t'* ]]; do d="${d#$'\t'}"; done; fi
+      if [[ "$d" == "$_hd_delim" ]]; then found=$j; break; fi
+    done
+    if (( found < 0 )); then _bdb_hd_class=interpreter; printf '%s' "${1:-}"; return; fi
+    cls="$_hd_cls"
+    (( ctx )) && cls=interpreter
+    _hd_pipe_saved="$_hd_pipe"
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
+      first="${_bdb_hd_L[i+1]:-}"
+      (( i + 1 < found )) || first=""
+      first="${first#"${first%%[![:blank:]]*}"}"
+      [[ "$first" == '#!'* ]] && cls=interpreter
+    fi
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]]; then
+      local -a dests
+      dests=(${_hd_dests[@]+"${_hd_dests[@]}"})
+      for d in ${dests[@]+"${dests[@]}"}; do
+        if _bdb_hd_exec_dest "$d" || _bdb_hd_same_line_exec "${d##*/}" "$i" $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)); then
+          cls=interpreter; break
+        fi
+      done
+    fi
+    _bdb_hd_scan_body $((i + 1)) $((found - 1)) "$_hd_quoted"
+    out="$out$l"$'\n'
+    if [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && (( ! _hd_full )); then
+      # #1245 special case: a standalone quoted `cat <<'W' [> path]` drops it all.
+      if ! (( i == 0 && found == _bdb_hd_n - 1 && _hd_quoted )) || ! _bdb_hd_plain_cat "$l"; then
+        out="$out$_hd_kept"
+      fi
+    else
+      [[ "$cls" == nonexec ]] && cls=interpreter
+      for ((j = i + 1; j < found; j++)); do out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[j]}"$'\n'; done
+      out="$out$_hd_synth"
+    fi
+    out="$out${_bdb_hd_L[found]}"$'\n'
+    (( ctx )) || ! _bdb_hd_ctx_bad "$l" || ctx=1
+    case "$cls" in
+      interpreter) seen=interpreter ;;
+      none) [[ "$seen" == interpreter ]] || seen=none ;;
+      nonexec) [[ -n "$seen" ]] || seen=nonexec ;;
+    esac
+    i=$((found + 1))
+  done
+  _bdb_hd_class="${seen:-none}"
+  printf '%s' "${out%$'\n'}"
+}
+
+# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).
+_bdb_hd_plain_cat() {
+  local header="${1:-}" marker candidate
+  local delimiter_re="<<(-?)('([[:alnum:]_]+)'|\"([[:alnum:]_]+)\")"
+  local path_re="([[:alnum:]_./-]+|'[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+'|\"[[:alnum:]_ ./-]+\")"
+  local header_re="^[[:blank:]]*cat[[:blank:]]+(HEREDOC([[:blank:]]+>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re})?|>>?[[:blank:]]*${path_re}[[:blank:]]+HEREDOC)[[:blank:]]*$"
+  [[ "$header" =~ $delimiter_re ]] || return 1
+  marker="${BASH_REMATCH[0]}"
+  candidate="${header/"$marker"/HEREDOC}"
+  [[ "$candidate" =~ $header_re ]]
+}

+# Knob: destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier in the repo's
+# .loa.config.yaml (read once, no fork, only for commands holding `<<`).
+# Only an explicit false|no|off turns it off; turning it off only tightens.
+_bdb_heredoc_knob_on() {
+  local cfg="${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}/.loa.config.yaml" content="" l in_blk=0
+  [[ -f "$cfg" && -r "$cfg" ]] || return 0
+  IFS= read -r -d '' content < "$cfg" || true
+  [[ "$content" == *heredoc_classifier* ]] || return 0
+  while IFS= read -r l; do
+    case "$l" in
+      destructive_command_guard:*) in_blk=1; continue ;;
+      [A-Za-z_]*) in_blk=0; continue ;;
+    esac
+    if (( in_blk )) && [[ "$l" =~ $_bdb_hd_re_knob ]]; then
+      case "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" in false|False|FALSE|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) return 1 ;; esac
+    fi
+  done <<< "$content"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# Exported entry points (source with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1).
+_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  local LC_ALL=C
+  _bdb_heredoc_scrub "${1:-}" >/dev/null
+  printf '%s\n' "$_bdb_hd_class"
+}
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}
+
+# Library mode: only when SOURCED. Executed with BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 the hook runs
+# normally — an environment variable can never switch the fence off.
+if [[ "${BDB_LIB_ONLY:-}" == "1" && "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" != "${0:-}" ]]; then
+  return 0
+fi

--- /dev/null
+++ b/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,308 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
+# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
+#
+# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
+# unless stated):
+#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
+#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
+#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
+#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
+#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
+#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
+#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
+#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
+#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
+#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
+#
+# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
+#
+# Inputs (each has a test seam):
+#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
+#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
+#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
+#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
+#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
+#
+# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
+# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
+# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
+# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
+# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
+# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
+# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
+#
+# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
+# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
+# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
+# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
+# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
+# =============================================================================
+
+_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
+_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
+[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
+_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
+_LOA_PL_JSON=""
+_LOA_PL_ID=""
+
+_loa_pl_paths() {
+  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
+  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
+    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
+  fi
+  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
+  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
+  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
+  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
+    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
+  fi
+  _LOA_PL_CFG="${LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE:-${status_cfg:-$default_cfg}}"
+  _LOA_PL_PROF="${LOA_PROFILES_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml}"
+  _LOA_PL_FLOOR="${LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE:-$root/.claude/data/floor.yaml}"
+  if [[ -n "${LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
+    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
+  elif [[ "$_LOA_PL_CFG" == "$default_cfg" ]]; then
+    _LOA_PL_CACHE="$root/.run/effective-config.json"
+  else
+    _LOA_PL_CACHE=""
+  fi
+}
+
+# The cache key: the three paths plus one stat line per existing file. An
+# empty stat output for an existing file (no usable stat) disables caching.
+_loa_pl_id() {
+  local st
+  st=$(stat -Lc '%n|%y|%s' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) ||
+    st=$(stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z' -- "$_LOA_PL_CFG" "$_LOA_PL_PROF" "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || true
+  if [[ -z "$st" ]] && [[ -e "$_LOA_PL_CFG" || -e "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
+    _LOA_PL_CUR_ID=""
+    return 0
+  fi
+  _LOA_PL_CUR_ID="v1|$_LOA_PL_CFG|$_LOA_PL_PROF|$_LOA_PL_FLOOR|${st//$'\n'/;}"
+}
+
+_loa_pl_warn() { printf '[profile-lib] WARN: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
+
+# Builds the resolved document from the three inputs into _LOA_PL_JSON.
+_loa_pl_build() {
+  local cfg='{}' prof='{}' floor='[]' out
+  if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
+    return 1
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_CFG" ]]; then
+    if ! cfg=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null); then
+      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_CFG does not parse; profile defaults apply"
+      cfg='{}'
+    fi
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_PROF" ]]; then
+    if ! prof=$(yq -o=json '.' "$_LOA_PL_PROF" 2>/dev/null); then
+      _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF does not parse; no profile defaults apply"
+      prof='{}'
+    fi
+  else
+    _loa_pl_warn "$_LOA_PL_PROF is missing; no profile defaults apply"
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" ]]; then
+    floor=$(yq -o=json '.floor_keys // []' "$_LOA_PL_FLOOR" 2>/dev/null) || floor='[]'
+  fi
+  [[ -n "$cfg" ]] || cfg='{}'
+  [[ -n "$prof" ]] || prof='{}'
+  [[ -n "$floor" ]] || floor='[]'
+  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$cfg" "$prof" "$floor" | jq -cs --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" '
+    def render: if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end;
+    def clean($n): render | gsub("[[:cntrl:]]"; "?") | .[0:$n];
+    def globre: "^" + (split("*") | map(gsub("\\."; "\\.")) | join(".+")) + "$";
+    (.[0] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cfg |
+    (.[1] | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pf |
+    (.[2] | if type == "array" then map(select(type == "string")) else [] end) as $floor |
+    ($pf.profiles | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $profiles |
+    ([$profiles[] | objects | keys[]] | unique) as $all |
+    def forbidden($k): any($floor[]; . as $f | ($k | test($f | globre)) or (($f | split("*")[0]) | startswith($k + ".")));
+    ($all | map(select(forbidden(.)))) as $bad |
+    ($all - $bad) as $keys |
+    (try ($cfg.loa.profile) catch null) as $req |
+    (if $req == null then {name: "standard", source: "default"}
+     elif ($req | type) == "string" and ($profiles[$req]? | type) == "object" then {name: $req, source: "explicit"}
+     else {name: "standard", source: "invalid"} end) as $sel |
+    ($profiles[$sel.name]? // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $pv |
+    (reduce $keys[] as $k ({};
+        (try ($cfg | getpath($k | split("."))) catch null) as $e |
+        (if ($pv | has($k)) then $pv[$k] else null end) as $p |
+        if $e != null then .[$k] = {value: $e, source: "explicit", profile_value: $p}
+        elif ($pv | has($k)) then .[$k] = {value: $p, source: "profile", profile_value: $p}
+        else . end)) as $knobs |
+    {
+      schema_version: 1,
+      id: $id,
+      profile: $sel.name,
+      profile_source: $sel.source,
+      profile_requested: (if $req == null then null else ($req | clean(64)) end),
+      profile_keys: $keys,
+      knobs: $knobs,
+      overrides: ([$knobs | to_entries[]
+                   | select(.value.source == "explicit" and .value.value != .value.profile_value)
+                   | "\(.key)=\(.value.value | clean(128))"] | sort),
+      warnings: ([if $sel.source == "invalid" then "unknown loa.profile \"\($req | clean(64))\"; using standard" else empty end]
+                 + [$bad[] | "profiles.yaml key \(.) names a floor key; ignored"])
+    }' 2>/dev/null) || out=""
+  if [[ -z "$out" ]]; then
+    _LOA_PL_JSON=""
+    return 1
+  fi
+  _LOA_PL_JSON="$out"
+  local w
+  while IFS= read -r w; do
+    [[ -n "$w" ]] && _loa_pl_warn "$w"
+  done < <(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.warnings[]?' 2>/dev/null)
+  return 0
+}
+
+_loa_pl_write_cache() {
+  [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" ]] || return 0
+  local dir="${_LOA_PL_CACHE%/*}" tmp
+  [[ "$dir" == "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] && dir="."
+  if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]]; then
+    mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
+  fi
+  tmp="$_LOA_PL_CACHE.tmp.$$"
+  if printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
+    mv -f "$tmp" "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
+  else
+    rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+# Loads the resolved document into _LOA_PL_JSON (memo → cache → build).
+# Returns 1 when it cannot be resolved (jq or yq missing).
+_loa_pl_load() {
+  _loa_pl_paths
+  _loa_pl_id
+  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && "$_LOA_PL_ID" == "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" ]]; then
+    return 0
+  fi
+  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
+  if [[ -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]]; then
+    local j
+    j=$(jq -c --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" 'if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then . else empty end' \
+        "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || j=""
+    if [[ -n "$j" ]]; then
+      _LOA_PL_JSON="$j"
+      _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  fi
+  _loa_pl_build || return 1
+  _LOA_PL_ID="$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID"
+  _loa_pl_write_cache
+  return 0
+}
+
+# Live read of one explicit key (non-profile keys, or no resolution available).
+_loa_pl_live() {
+  local key="$1" fallback="$2" v
+  if [[ -f "${_LOA_PL_CFG:-}" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    v=$(yq -o=json ".$key" "$_LOA_PL_CFG" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if . == null then "__LOA_PL_MISS__" elif type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end' 2>/dev/null) || v=""
+    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$v"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  fi
+  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
+  return 0
+}
+
+loa_knob() {
+  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
+  key="${path#.}"
+  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
+    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
+    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
+    return 2
+  fi
+  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
+  _loa_pl_paths
+  _loa_pl_id
+  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
+     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
+          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
+            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
+               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
+             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
+          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
+    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
+      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
+      return 0
+    fi
+    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$v"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  fi
+  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
+    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
+        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
+          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
+        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
+  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
+    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  printf '%s\n' "$v"
+  return 0
+}
+
+loa_profile() {
+  if _loa_pl_load; then
+    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
+  else
+    echo standard
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+loa_profile_source() {
+  if _loa_pl_load; then
+    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
+  else
+    echo default
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+loa_profile_overrides() {
+  if _loa_pl_load; then
+    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.overrides[]?' 2>/dev/null || true
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+loa_effective_json() {
+  if _loa_pl_load; then
+    printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON"
+  else
+    echo '{}'
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
+  export LC_ALL=C
+  case "${1:-}" in
+    profile)   loa_profile ;;
+    source)    loa_profile_source ;;
+    knob)      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "usage: profile-lib.sh knob <yq-path> [fallback]" >&2; exit 2; }
+               loa_knob "$2" "${3:-}"; exit $? ;;
+    overrides) loa_profile_overrides ;;
+    json)      loa_effective_json ;;
+    *)         sed -n '3,/^# =====/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+fi

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Invariant 4b: optional constraint tables appear exactly when their class has
+# rows (cycle-129 D-4.5). generate-constraints.sh omits the "## Agent Teams"
+# table when constraints.json has no agent_teams_constraints rows; the kernel
+# must then carry neither the heading nor the marker, and must carry the
+# marker whenever the rows exist.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+check_optional_constraint_tables() {
+  local file=".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" registry=".claude/data/constraints.json"
+  [[ -f "$file" && -f "$registry" ]] || return 0
+  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
+  jq empty "$registry" 2>/dev/null || return 0   # invariant 3 reports invalid JSON
+
+  local entry section heading rows has_marker has_heading
+  for entry in "agent_teams_constraints|## Agent Teams"; do
+    IFS='|' read -r section heading <<< "$entry"
+    rows=$(jq --arg s "$section" '[.constraints[]? | select(any(.layers[]?; .section == $s))] | length' "$registry" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    has_marker=0; has_heading=0
+    grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section} " "$file" 2>/dev/null && has_marker=1
+    grep -qxF "$heading" "$file" 2>/dev/null && has_heading=1
+    if [[ "$rows" -eq 0 && ( "$has_marker" -eq 1 || "$has_heading" -eq 1 ) ]]; then
+      report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "${section}: constraints.json has no rows but CLAUDE.loa.md still carries the '${heading}' table — run generate-constraints.sh"
+    elif [[ "$rows" -gt 0 && "$has_marker" -eq 0 ]]; then
+      report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "${section}: constraints.json has ${rows} row(s) but CLAUDE.loa.md has no ${section} block — restore the '${heading}' heading block, then run generate-constraints.sh"
+    else
+      report "PASS" "constraint-blocks" "${section}: table presence matches constraints.json (${rows} row(s))"
+    fi
+  done
+}
+
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Invariant 5: Required files present
 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@@ -564,6 +594,7 @@ check_system_zone
 check_claude_md
 check_constraints

+check_optional_constraint_tables
 check_required_files
 check_hook_executables
 check_hooks_json

     echo ""

@@ -931,6 +936,31 @@ display_providers_section() {
   return 0
 }
 
+# cycle-129 FR-9 (SDD D-9.3): one Profile line — the effective loa.profile and
+# the explicit keys whose value differs from it. Reads the config the Providers
+# block reads (bats-gated seam LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE); the lib runs in a
+# subshell so its globals stay out of this script.
+display_profile_line() {
+  local lib="$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/profile-lib.sh" cfg line
+  if [[ ! -f "$lib" ]]; then
+    echo -e "${BOLD}Profile:${NC} unknown (lib/profile-lib.sh missing; reinstall the framework with /update-loa)"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  cfg=$(_providers_config_file)
+  line=$(
+    if [[ "$cfg" != "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$cfg"; fi
+    # shellcheck source=lib/profile-lib.sh
+    source "$lib" || exit 0
+    name=$(loa_profile 2>/dev/null) || name=standard
+    note=""
+    if [[ "$(loa_profile_source 2>/dev/null)" == "invalid" ]]; then note="unknown loa.profile, using standard; "; fi
+    ov=$(loa_profile_overrides 2>/dev/null | awk 'NF { printf "%s%s", (n++ ? ", " : ""), $0 }')

+}

 # register (grimoires/loa/guards.md), the 30-day yield from the untracked
 # .run/guard-yield.json; nothing is recomputed here. Bats-gated seams:
@@ -978,6 +1008,25 @@ display_gate_line() {

 }
 
+# cycle-129 FR-5 / FR-4(a) (SDD D-5.3): the run position the files derive against
+# the cache (`run-checkpoint.sh derive --json` — report-only, /loa writes no state;
+# printed only on drift) and the implement gate's effective mode, from the gate's
+# own parser. Bats-gated seams: LOA_STATUS_DERIVE_ROOT, LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE.
+display_run_position_lines() {
+  local ck="${SCRIPT_DIR}/run-checkpoint.sh" gate="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh"
+  local root="$PROJECT_ROOT" dj line mode
+  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" && -n "${LOA_STATUS_DERIVE_ROOT:-}" ]]; then root="$LOA_STATUS_DERIVE_ROOT"; fi
+  if [[ -f "$ck" ]] && dj=$(bash "$ck" derive --json --root "$root" 2>/dev/null) \

+                       | "files say \(.state | tostring | gsub("[^A-Z_]"; "")), cache said \(.cache_state | tostring | gsub("[^A-Z_]"; ""))"' <<<"$dj" 2>/dev/null); then
+    echo "  Run: $line (drift) → run-checkpoint.sh derive --write"
+  fi

+    echo "  Gate: implement_gate.mode $mode"

+### Heredoc consumer classification (cycle-129 FR-6)
+
+Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
+
+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
+- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Their bodies are scanned per segment. Segments that start with a fence verb are kept for the normal rules, and the rest are dropped. A substitution under an unquoted delimiter, an interpreter word or a variable command word sends the body back to a full scan.
+- **Default.** A consumer on neither list, or a parse failure, scans in full. The #1245 quoted standalone `cat` scrub is the special case and is also the knob-off path.
+- **Export.** Source the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and call `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command>`, which prints `interpreter`, `nonexec` or `none`. `heredoc_nonexec <command>` exits 0 for a non-executing heredoc. Library mode applies only when the file is sourced. An executed hook ignores the variable.
+- **Remaining gap.** A body written to a plain file by one command and executed by a later command is outside a per-command fence. The Write tool shares this limit.
+
 **Accepted false positives (quote-blindness residue, cycle-120 C-D3)**: the inert-carrier scrub redacts a known data carrier's value (git commit `-m`, `br`/`bd -d`, `gh … create --body/--title`, `echo`/`printf`) only when the value holds **neither `$(` nor a backtick**. A lone `$` (dollar amount, `$ENV` mention, trailing bare `$`) is now permitted inside a redacted value — so `git commit -m "saved $5 by dropping find . -exec rm -rf {} +"` correctly ALLOWs. One residual false positive is **accepted by design**:
 
 - **Case A — a `$(…)` command-substitution inside a carrier value** (e.g. a multi-line commit body wrapped in `$(cat <<'EOF' … find -exec rm -rf … EOF)`). The `$(` disqualifies the value from redaction (a regex fence cannot parse subshell contents without reintroducing the #1047 bypass), so a destructive *shape* mentioned inside that subshell body still trips FR-2 and blocks a genuinely safe commit. **Workaround**: paraphrase the destructive shape in the commit body (as the cycle-119 commits did — e.g. write "find-exec-rm" rather than the literal `find … -exec rm -rf`), or drop the `$(…)` wrapper. This is a preserved false positive, never a bypass: leaving `$(`/backtick values un-redacted is what keeps command-substitution smuggling (`git commit -m "$(rm -rf /)"`) caught. Backtick command-substitution itself remains the separately-tracked, uncaught pre-existing gap (bd-bdb-backtick-bypass).

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
+# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
+# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
+# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
+# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
+#
+#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
+#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
+#                                           all have non-executing consumers
+#
+# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
+# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
+# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
+_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
+if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
+fi
+unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence
+
+heredoc_consumer_class() {
+  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
+  else
+    printf 'none\n'
+  fi
+}
+
+heredoc_nonexec() {
+  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
+}

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

readonly SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
readonly SCRIPT_NAME="$(basename "$0")"
readonly PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
readonly SKILLS_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills"
readonly CONFIG_FILE="$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
readonly TRAJECTORY_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory"

# Require bash 4.0+ (associative arrays)
# shellcheck source=bash-version-guard.sh
        esac
    done

    # Validate required arguments
    if [[ -z "$skill" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --skill is required" >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    if [[ -z "$mode" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --mode is required" >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    if [[ "$mode" != "interactive" && "$mode" != "autonomous" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --mode must be 'interactive' or 'autonomous'" >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    # Check if enforcement is enabled
    if ! is_enforcement_enabled; then
        # Use jq for safe JSON output (M-5 fix)
        jq -n \
            --arg action "PROCEED" \
            --arg skill "$skill" \
            --arg level "unknown" \
            --arg mode "$mode" \
            --arg reason "danger level enforcement disabled in config" \
            --argjson log false \
            --argjson override_used false \
            '{action: $action, skill: $skill, level: $level, mode: $mode, reason: $reason, log: $log, override_used: $override_used}'
        exit 0
    fi

    # Get danger level for skill
    local level
    level=$(get_danger_level "$skill")

    # Enforce based on mode
    local result
    local action
    local reason

    if [[ "$mode" == "interactive" ]]; then
        result=$(enforce_interactive "$skill" "$level")
    else
        result=$(enforce_autonomous "$skill" "$level" "$allow_high")
    fi

    action=$(echo "$result" | head -1)
    reason=$(echo "$result" | tail -1)
        exit 1
    fi

    if [[ -z "$input" ]]; then
        echo "Error: --input or --file is required" >&2
        exit 1
    fi

    # Check if guardrails are enabled
    if ! is_enabled; then
        cat <<EOF
{
  "action": "PROCEED",
  "skill": "$skill",
  "mode": "$mode",
  "checks": [],
  "reason": "guardrails disabled in config",
  "latency_ms": 0
}
EOF
        exit 0
    fi

    # Run all checks
    local checks=()
    local redacted_input="$input"

+# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# PreToolUse check on Write/Edit/NotebookEdit into the App Zone (src/, lib/, app/)
+# outside an implementation run. A write is SANCTIONED (allowed, one audit row each) by:

+      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
+      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
+      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
+      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
+      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
+      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
+      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
+      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
+      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
+       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
+       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
+       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
+       commit_after_verdict: (if ($c | length) == 2 and $vts != null
+                              then (($c[1] | tonumber) > ($vts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0)) else null end),
+       legacy_feedback: ([$rv, $au] | map(select(.exists and (.trailer | not)) | .file)),
+       state: (if $M and $R and $A and $status == "completed" then "complete"
+               elif ($M | not) and $R and $A then "awaiting_marker" else "in_progress" end)}')
+    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")
+  done <<<"$rows"
+
+  # Breaker recompute over the active sprint's ordered rounds
+  local active_gid rounds cache="null" cache_ok=1 bcache="null" reset rc merged
+  active_gid=$(jq -r 'if length == 0 then "" else ((map(select(.state != "complete")) | .[0]) // .[-1]) | .global_id | tostring end' <<<"$sprints")
+  rounds="[]"
+  if [[ -n "$active_gid" && -d "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" ]]; then
+    rounds=$(rounds_of "$a2a/sprint-$active_gid" | jq -sc '.')
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
+    if cache=$(jq -c . "$file" 2>/dev/null) && [[ -n "$cache" ]]; then :; else cache="null"; cache_ok=0; fi
+  fi
+  if [[ -f "$breaker" ]]; then bcache=$(jq -c 'if type == "object" then . else null end' "$breaker" 2>/dev/null) || bcache="null"; [[ -n "$bcache" ]] || bcache="null"; fi
+  reset=$(jq -c '.reset_at? // null | if type == "string" then . else null end' <<<"$bcache")
+  rc=$(jq -nc --argjson r "$rounds" --argjson z "$reset" "$JQ_DEFS"' recompute($r; $z)')
+  merged=$(jq -c --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' <<<"$bcache")
+
+  local facts report
+  facts=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$sprints" --argjson b "$merged" '
+    {sprints: $s,
+     all_complete: (($s | length) > 0 and all($s[]; .state == "complete")),
+     breaker_open: ($b.state == "OPEN"),
+     stale_markers: [$s[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id)"],
+     legacy_feedback: [$s[] | .legacy_feedback[]],
+     sprint_ids: [$s[] | "sprint-\(.global_id)"]}')
+  report=$(jq -nc --argjson f "$facts" --argjson c "$cache" --argjson b "$merged" --argjson rc "$rc" \
+                  --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" --arg cycle "$active" \
+                  --argjson fa "$fa" --argjson cache_ok "$cache_ok" --arg ag "$active_gid" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    def st: if type == "string" then (if test("^[A-Z_]{1,32}$") then . else "INVALID" end) else null end;
+    ($c | resolve($f; $now; $win)) as $s
+    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.state | st) else null end) as $cs
+    | ($c | if type == "object" then (.status | st) else null end) as $cst
+    | {cycle: $cycle, derived_at: $ts, stale_hours: ($win / 3600), file_authoritative: ($fa == 1),
+       state: $s, cache_state: $cs, cache_status: $cst,
+       cache: (if $cache_ok == 0 then "unparseable" elif $c == null then "missing" else "present" end),
+       drift: ($c != null and ($cs != $s or ($cst != null and $cst != $s))),
+       notes: ([
+         (if $cs != null and $cst != null and $cs != $cst then "cache .state \($cs) and .status \($cst) disagree" else empty end),
+         (if $s == "JACKED_OUT" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "JACKED_OUT is terminal: files show incomplete sprints; the cache is kept" else empty end),
+         (if $s == "COMPLETE" and ($f.all_complete | not) then "COMPLETE kept: no new incomplete sprint in the ledger" else empty end),
+         ($f.sprints[] | select(.stale_marker) | "sprint-\(.global_id): COMPLETED marker names another sprint (stale_marker, not counted)"),
+         ($f.sprints[] | select(.state == "awaiting_marker") | "sprint-\(.global_id): review and audit APPROVED, no COMPLETED marker")
+       ]),
+       sprints: $f.sprints,
+       active_sprint: (if $ag == "" then null else "sprint-\($ag)" end),
+       breaker: {state: $b.state, cycle_count: $b.triggers.cycle_count.current, same_issue: $b.triggers.same_issue.count,
+                 no_progress: $b.triggers.no_progress.count, recomputed: {cycle_count: $rc.cycle, same_issue: $rc.same, no_progress: $rc.np}},
+       derivation: {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback},
+       written: false}')
+
+  if (( write )); then
+    local why=""
+    if (( fa == 0 )); then why="run_mode.file_authoritative: false — report-only"
+    elif [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then why="no run state at $file — nothing to rewrite"
+    elif (( cache_ok == 0 )); then why="$file unparseable — kept for inspection, not rewritten"
+    fi
+    if [[ -z "$why" ]]; then
+      atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson rc "$rc" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"' merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts)' || return 3
+      merged=$(jq -c . "$breaker")
+      facts=$(jq -c --argjson b "$merged" '.breaker_open = ($b.state == "OPEN")' <<<"$facts")
+      atomic_update "$file" --argjson f "$facts" --argjson now "$now" --argjson win "$win" --arg ts "$now_ts" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+        resolve($f; $now; $win) as $s
+        | .state = $s | .status = $s | .derived_at = $ts
+        | .derivation = {source: "files", stale_markers: $f.stale_markers, legacy_feedback: $f.legacy_feedback, sprint_ids: $f.sprint_ids}
+        | .schema_version = (.schema_version // 2)' || return 3
+      report=$(jq -c --slurpfile c "$file" --argjson b "$merged" '.written = true | .state = $c[0].state | .breaker.state = $b.state' <<<"$report")
+    else
+      report=$(jq -c --arg w "$why" '.notes += [$w]' <<<"$report")
+    fi
+  fi

+  if (( json )); then
+    jq . <<<"$report"
+  else
+    jq -r '"derive: files say \(.state), cache said \(.cache_state // "nothing") (\(if .drift then "drift" else "in sync" end))"
+           + (if .written then " — caches rewritten" else "" end), (.notes[] | "  note: " + .)' <<<"$report"
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+cmd_record_round() {
+  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
+  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
+  local p th ts now out trip
+  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
+  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
+    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
+              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
+              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
+              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
+              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
+  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
+  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
+      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
+    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
+    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
+    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
+       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
+    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
+       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
+       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
+    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
+    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
+    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
+    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
+          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
+        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
+          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
+        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
+          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
+        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
+          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
+        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
+        else null end ) as $trip
+    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
+    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
+      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
+      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
+      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
+    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
+  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
+  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
+  echo "$out"
+  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
+    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
+    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
+    return 10
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+cmd_mark() {
+  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
+  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
+  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
+    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3
+  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
+    local err drc=0
+    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
+    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
+  fi
+  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
+}
+
 case "$sub" in
-  write) cmd_write ;;
-  read)  cmd_read ;;
+  write)  cmd_write ;;
+  read)   cmd_read ;;
+  derive) cmd_derive ;;
+  record-round) cmd_record_round ;;
+  mark)   cmd_mark ;;
+  unmark) rm -f -- "$run_dir/implement-active.json" "$run_dir/implement-active.json.lock"; echo "unmarked" ;;
   *) usage ;;
 esac

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
#
# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
}

# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
checkpoint() {
    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
}

# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
write_lines() {
    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
        | bash "$HOOK"
}

@test "KS-1 the counter resets when the checkpoint task changes" {
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-aaa
    write_lines 3
    write_lines 2
    [ "$(jq -r '.task' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "bd-aaa" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "5" ]
    checkpoint sprint-256 bd-bbb

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
#
# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
}

# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
checkpoint() {
    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
}

# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
write_lines() {
    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
        | bash "$HOOK"
}

## Main Loop — Single Sprint (`/run sprint-N`)

```
while circuit_breaker.state == CLOSED:
  1. /implement $target
  2. Commit changes, then track deletions (see "Deleted Files Tracking" below)
  3. update_state(phase: REVIEW); checkpoint(phase: REVIEW)
  4. /review-sprint $target
  5. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate review` on engineer-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` (anything else — including an inconsistent trailer — counts as
     findings) → record-round (see "Circuit Breaker" below); exit 10, HALT; else continue
     loop (back to step 1)
  6. update_state(phase: AUDIT); checkpoint(phase: AUDIT)
  7. /audit-sprint $target
  8. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate audit` on auditor-sprint-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` → same as step 5 (golden-path's `_gp_sprint_is_audited` additionally
     re-derives the review trailer and cross-checks `excluded` ⇔ `excluded_confirmed`)
  9. RED_TEAM_CODE gate (if enabled) — see resources/conditional-procedures.md §red-team-code-gate
  10. If COMPLETED marker exists → update_state(state: COMPLETE); break
Create draft PR (see "Completion and PR Creation" — resources/completion-modes.md)
Invoke Post-PR Validation if enabled — resources/conditional-procedures.md §post-pr-validation
Update state to READY_FOR_HITL or JACKED_OUT
```

Call `check_rate_limit` (see "Rate Limiting" below) before each of steps 1, 4, and 7.
`checkpoint(...)` = `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint $target --phase <PHASE>`
(when `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` exists); `/implement` writes the per-task checkpoint on each
`br close`. Beads stay the recovery truth — the checkpoint is a hint `/run-resume` reports.

content.text:
This PR can't merge: I found nine defects, and the most serious lets dangerous commands through the destructive-command check. The review is in `/workspace/review.md` (nine findings, then `Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`).

Six of the nine I reproduced by running the head and base scripts in a scratch directory; the other three come from reading the code.

**Most serious (reproduced):**
1. **The new heredoc check fails open** (`block-destructive-bash.sh:631`, `:216`). If a heredoc writes a file and the same command then pipes it to a shell through a "safe reader" (`cat n.txt | sh`), the command is classed as non-executing. Lines in the file that the System-Zone rules would block (`cp`, `mv`, `tee`, `sed -i`, redirects into `.claude/`) are dropped before those rules run. A case the base hook blocked (exit 2) is now allowed (exit 0). Running the file without naming it exactly (`sh pay*`, `make`, `sh -c "$(cat f)"`) also gets through.
2. **A routine checkpoint can halt a run** (`run-checkpoint.sh:280`). Older feedback files without a verdict trailer are counted as rejected rounds, and they all get the same issue hash. Three "All good" files plus one `run-checkpoint.sh write` trip the circuit breaker and set the run to HALTED, while the command still exits 0 and prints nothing.
3. **A breaker file created by `derive` has no thresholds, limit or timeout start time** (`run-checkpoint.sh:295`). The 8-hour timeout can then never fire for that run.
4. **The profile cache goes stale** (`profile-lib.sh:78`). If floor.yaml or the config file is missing, the cache key falls back to filesystem free-block counts instead of the file's modification time and size. Switching `lean` to `full` kept returning the old lean values.
5. **`derive` breaks on jq 1.6** (`run-checkpoint.sh:378`, `:226`). Using `$label` as a variable name is a syntax error there, and an empty-input check passes when it shouldn't. On jq 1.6 (still the version Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 12 ship) every `derive` fails, and `write`/`mark` report a misleading "not valid JSON" while exiting 0.

**From reading the code:**
- **The karpathy per-task counter is off by one task** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131`). The checkpoint names the last *closed* bead, so lines written for task N+1 are counted under task N's id. The review step that reads these files per bead therefore blames the wrong bead. The test misses this because its fake `br` reports every bead as closed. It also runs `run-checkpoint.sh read` and `br show` on every Write/Edit.
- **The retrospective quietly turns on for this repository** (`profiles.yaml:42`). The `standard` profile enables `invisible_retrospective`, but this repo's config never sets the key, and the old reader only ran on an explicit `true`. The PR pins the guardrail keys in the config but not this one.

I also ran the PR's new bats suites against a copy of the head tree. Many fail, but the causes look like files missing from this snapshot (for example `verdict-derive.sh`), jq 1.6, or an old bats, so I didn't cite any test result as evidence.
